sanskrit: tasya kruddhasya vadanaṃ dṛṣṭvā rāmasya dhīmataḥ sarvabhūtāni vitreṣuḥ prākampata ca medinī
english: Beholding the face of wise Rāma blazing with fury, all living beings trembled with fear, and the earth itself shook.

sanskrit: siṃhaśārdūlavāñ śailaḥ saṃcacālācaladrumaḥ babhūva cāpi kṣubhitaḥ samudraḥ saritāṃ patiḥ
english: A mountain haunted by lions and tigers trembled, its trees shaking though it stood still; the ocean, lord of rivers, was likewise thrown into turmoil.

sanskrit: khagāś ca kharanirghoṣā gagane paruṣasvanāḥ autpātikā vinardantaḥ samantāt paricakramuḥ
english: Birds with harsh cries and rough voices, portending ill omens, screamed and wheeled about on every side across the sky.

sanskrit: rāmaṃ dṛṣṭvā susaṃkruddham utpātāṃś ca sudāruṇān vitreṣuḥ sarvabhūtāni rāvaṇasyāviśad bhayam
english: Seeing Rāma seething with rage and witnessing those dreadful portents, all creatures were seized with terror, and fear entered into Rāvaṇa.

sanskrit: vimānasthās tadā devā gandharvāś ca mahoragāḥ ṛṣidānavadaityāś ca garutmantaś ca khecarāḥ
english: At that moment the gods standing in their celestial cars, the Gandharvas and great serpents, the sages, Dānavas, and Daityas, the Garutmats and sky-dwellers—

sanskrit: dadṛśus te tadā yuddhaṃ lokasaṃvartasaṃsthitam nānāpraharaṇair bhīmaiḥ śūrayoś ca saṃprayudhyatoḥ
english: —all witnessed that battle, which had the character of a cosmic dissolution, as the two heroes fought each other with many fearsome weapons.

sanskrit: ūcuḥ surāsurāḥ sarve tadā vigraham āgatāḥ prekṣamāṇā mahāyuddhaṃ vākyaṃ bhaktyā prahṛṣṭavat
english: All the gods and asuras assembled to witness the conflict, and beholding the great battle, spoke words of joyful devotion.

sanskrit: daśagrīvaṃ jayety āhur asurāḥ samavasthitāḥ devā rāmam athocus te tvaṃ jayeti punaḥ punaḥ
english: The assembled asuras cried "Victory to Daśagrīva!", while the gods cried out to Rāma again and again, "Victory to you!"

sanskrit: etasminn antare krodhād rāghavasya sa rāvaṇaḥ prahartukāmo duṣṭātmā spṛśan praharaṇaṃ mahat
english: Meanwhile, that wicked-souled Rāvaṇa, enraged at Rāghava and eager to strike, laid hold of a great weapon—

sanskrit: vajrasāraṃ mahānādaṃ sarvaśatrunibarhaṇam śailaśṛṅganibhaiḥ kūṭaiś citaṃ dṛṣṭibhayāvaham
english: —a spear with the hardness of the thunderbolt, resounding mightily, the destroyer of all foes, adorned with tips like mountain peaks, terrifying to behold—

sanskrit: sadhūmam iva tīkṣṇāgraṃ yugāntāgnicayopamam atiraudram anāsādyaṃ kālenāpi durāsadam
english: —with sharp points as though wreathed in smoke, comparable to the fire at the end of a cosmic age, supremely terrible, unapproachable, difficult to withstand even for Death himself—

sanskrit: trāsanaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ dāraṇaṃ bhedanaṃ tathā pradīpta iva roṣeṇa śūlaṃ jagrāha rāvaṇaḥ
english: —a trident that inspired terror in all beings, that split and pierced. Rāvaṇa seized it, blazing as it were with his own fury.

sanskrit: tac chūlaṃ paramakruddho madhye jagrāha vīryavān anekaiḥ samare śūrai rākṣasaiḥ parivāritaḥ
english: Supremely enraged, that mighty one grasped the trident by its middle, surrounded in battle by many valiant rākṣasas.

sanskrit: samudyamya mahākāyo nanāda yudhi bhairavam saṃraktanayano roṣāt svasainyam abhiharṣayan
english: Raising it aloft, that great-bodied one let out a fearsome battle-roar, his eyes red with rage, exhilarating his own army.

sanskrit: pṛthivīṃ cāntarikṣaṃ ca diśaś ca pradiśas tathā prākampayat tadā śabdo rākṣasendrasya dāruṇaḥ
english: That dreadful roar of the lord of rākṣasas caused the earth, the atmosphere, the cardinal directions, and the intermediate directions to tremble.

sanskrit: atinādasya nādena tena tasya durātmanaḥ sarvabhūtāni vitreṣuḥ sāgaraś ca pracukṣubhe
english: At that tremendous roar of the evil-souled one, all living creatures trembled and the ocean was thrown into agitation.

sanskrit: sa gṛhītvā mahāvīryaḥ śūlaṃ tad rāvaṇo mahat vinadya sumahānādaṃ rāmaṃ paruṣam abravīt
english: Taking up that great trident in his might, Rāvaṇa uttered a tremendous cry and spoke harsh words to Rāma:

sanskrit: śūlo 'yaṃ vajrasāras te rāma roṣān mayodyataḥ tava bhrātṛsahāyasya sadyaḥ prāṇān hariṣyati
english: "This spear, Rāma, hard as the thunderbolt, raised by me in fury, shall instantly snatch away the life of you together with your brother and allies."

sanskrit: rakṣasām adya śūrāṇāṃ nihatānāṃ camūmukhe tvāṃ nihatya raṇaślāghin karomi tarasā samam
english: "Having slain you today, O boaster in battle, I shall swiftly even the score for the valiant rākṣasas slain at the forefront of the army."

sanskrit: tiṣṭhedānīṃ nihanmi tvām eṣa śūlena rāghava evam uktvā sa cikṣepa tac chūlaṃ rākṣasādhipaḥ
english: "Stand now — I shall slay you with this trident, O Rāghava!" Having spoken thus, the lord of rākṣasas hurled that trident.

sanskrit: āpatantaṃ śaraugheṇa vārayām āsa rāghavaḥ utpatantaṃ yugāntāgniṃ jalaughair iva vāsavaḥ
english: Rāghava checked that oncoming trident with a volley of arrows, even as Vāsava checks a rising fire at the end of the age with a deluge of water.

sanskrit: nirdadāha sa tān bāṇān rāmakārmukaniḥsṛtān rāvaṇasya mahāśūlaḥ pataṃgān iva pāvakaḥ
english: But Rāvaṇa's great trident burned up those arrows shot from Rāma's bow, just as fire burns up moths.

sanskrit: tān dṛṣṭvā bhasmasād bhūtāñ śūlasaṃsparśacūrṇitān sāyakān antarikṣasthān rāghavaḥ krodham āharat
english: Seeing those arrows reduced to ash, pulverized by contact with the trident while still in midair, Rāghava took hold of his wrath.

sanskrit: sa tāṃ mātalinānītāṃ śaktiṃ vāsavanirmitām jagrāha paramakruddho rāghavo raghunandanaḥ
english: Supremely enraged, Rāghava, the joy of the Raghu line, seized the śakti-weapon brought by Mātali and fashioned by Vāsava.

sanskrit: sā tolitā balavatā śaktir ghaṇṭākṛtasvanā nabhaḥ prajvālayām āsa yugāntolkeva saprabhā
english: Swung by the mighty one, the śakti rang like a bell and blazed across the sky, radiant as a comet at the end of a cosmic age.

sanskrit: sā kṣiptā rākṣasendrasya tasmiñ śūle papāta ha bhinnaḥ śaktyā mahāñ śūlo nipapāta gatadyutiḥ
english: Hurled against the lord of rākṣasas, it struck that trident; shattered by the śakti, the great trident fell, its brilliance gone.

sanskrit: nirbibheda tato bāṇair hayān asya mahājavān rāmas tīkṣṇair mahāvegair vajrakalpaiḥ śitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Then Rāma pierced his swift horses with sharp arrows — swift, powerfully driven, keen, comparable to thunderbolts.

sanskrit: nirbibhedorasi tadā rāvaṇaṃ niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ rāghavaḥ paramāyatto lalāṭe patribhis tribhiḥ
english: Then Rāghava, fully focused, pierced Rāvaṇa in the chest with sharp arrows, and struck him on the forehead with three arrow-shafts.

sanskrit: sa śarair bhinnasarvāṅgo gātraprasrutaśoṇitaḥ rākṣasendraḥ samūhasthaḥ phullāśoka ivābabhau
english: His entire body pierced by arrows, blood flowing from his limbs, the lord of rākṣasas standing amid his host appeared like a blossoming aśoka tree.

sanskrit: sa rāmabāṇair atividdhagātro niśācarendraḥ kṣatajārdragātraḥ jagāma khedaṃ ca samājamadhye krodhaṃ ca cakre subhṛśaṃ tadānīm
english: His body pierced through and through by Rāma's arrows, his limbs wet with blood, the lord of night-stalkers felt distress in the midst of the assembly and then burned with intense rage.

sanskrit: sa tu tena tadā krodhāt kākutsthenārdito raṇe rāvaṇaḥ samaraślāghī mahākrodham upāgamat
english: Then Rāvaṇa, that boaster in battle, tormented in combat by Kākutstha with such fury, was overcome by towering rage.

sanskrit: sa dīptanayano roṣāc cāpam āyamya vīryavān abhyardayat susaṃkruddho rāghavaṃ paramāhave
english: His eyes blazing with anger, that mighty one drew his bow and, filled with violent fury, assailed Rāghava in the supreme clash.

sanskrit: bāṇadhārāsahasrais tu sa toyada ivāmbarāt rāghavaṃ rāvaṇo bāṇais taṭākam iva pūrayat
english: With thousands of streams of arrows, Rāvaṇa filled Rāghava with shafts like a cloud from the sky filling a lake.

sanskrit: pūritaḥ śarajālena dhanurmuktena saṃyuge mahāgirir ivākampyaḥ kākustho na prakampate
english: Though filled with a net of arrows released from the bow in combat, Kākutstha did not waver — like a great mountain, immovable.

sanskrit: sa śaraiḥ śarajālāni vārayan samare sthitaḥ gabhastīn iva sūryasya pratijagrāha vīryavān
english: Standing firm in battle, warding off showers of arrows with his own arrows, that mighty one received them as the sun receives its own rays.

sanskrit: tataḥ śarasahasrāṇi kṣiprahasto niśācaraḥ nijaghānorasi kruddho rāghavasya mahātmanaḥ
english: Then the night-stalker, quick-handed and enraged, struck great-souled Rāghava in the chest with thousands of arrows.

sanskrit: sa śoṇitasamādigdhaḥ samare lakṣmaṇāgrajaḥ dṛṣṭaḥ phulla ivāraṇye sumahān kiṃśukadrumaḥ
english: Smeared with blood in battle, Lakṣmaṇa's elder brother appeared like a great kiṃśuka tree in full bloom in the forest.

sanskrit: śarābhighātasaṃrabdhaḥ so 'pi jagrāha sāyakān kākutsthaḥ sumahātejā yugāntādityavarcasaḥ
english: Roused to fury by the impact of arrows, Kākutstha — of very great splendour, radiant as the sun at the end of the age — seized his own arrows in turn.

sanskrit: tato 'nyonyaṃ susaṃrabdhāv ubhau tau rāmarāvaṇau śarāndhakāre samare nopālakṣayatāṃ tadā
english: Then those two — Rāma and Rāvaṇa — deeply enraged with each other, could no longer make each other out in that battle amid the darkness of arrows.

sanskrit: tataḥ krodhasamāviṣṭo rāmo daśarathātmajaḥ uvāca rāvaṇaṃ vīraḥ prahasya paruṣaṃ vacaḥ
english: Then Rāma, son of Daśaratha, possessed by wrath, spoke harsh words to Rāvaṇa with a contemptuous laugh:

sanskrit: mama bhāryā janasthānād ajñānād rākṣasādhama hṛtā te vivaśā yasmāt tasmāt tvaṃ nāsi vīryavān
english: "Because you abducted my helpless wife from Janasthāna by stealth, O vilest of rākṣasas, you are therefore no hero."

sanskrit: mayā virahitāṃ dīnāṃ vartamānāṃ mahāvane vaidehīṃ prasabhaṃ hṛtvā śūro 'ham iti manyase
english: "You forcibly carried off Vaidehī, wretched and separated from me, dwelling in the great forest — and you think yourself a hero?"

sanskrit: strīṣu śūra vināthāsu paradārābhimarśake kṛtvā kāpuruṣaṃ karma śūro 'ham iti manyase
english: "You are a hero against defenceless women, a violator of another's wife — having done the deed of a coward, you think yourself a hero?"

sanskrit: bhinnamaryāda nirlajja cāritreṣv anavasthita darpān mṛtyum upādāya śūro 'ham iti manyase
english: "Transgressor of all bounds, shameless one, unstable in conduct — you have embraced death through arrogance and still you think yourself a hero?"

sanskrit: śūreṇa dhanadabhrātrā balaiḥ samuditena ca ślāghanīyaṃ yaśasyaṃ ca kṛtaṃ karma mahat tvayā
english: "What you did with the help of your heroic brother Dhanada and his forces is indeed glorious and praiseworthy — what a great deed!"

sanskrit: utsekenābhipannasya garhitasyāhitasya ca karmaṇaḥ prāpnuhīdānīṃ tasyādya sumahat phalam
english: "Now reap today the very great fruit of that deed — a deed approached through arrogance, a deed that is contemptible and harmful."

sanskrit: śūro 'ham iti cātmānam avagacchasi durmate naiva lajjāsti te sītāṃ coravad vyapakarṣataḥ
english: "You reckon yourself a hero, O evil-minded one, yet you feel no shame at having dragged away Sītā like a thief."

sanskrit: yadi matsaṃnidhau sītā dharṣitā syāt tvayā balāt bhrātaraṃ tu kharaṃ paśyes tadā matsāyakair hataḥ
english: "Had you violated Sītā by force in my presence, you would then have beheld your brother Khara slain by my arrows."

sanskrit: diṣṭyāsi mama duṣṭātmaṃś cakṣurviṣayam āgataḥ adya tvāṃ sāyakais tīkṣṇair nayāmi yamasādanam
english: "Fortunately, O evil-souled one, you have come within the range of my sight — today I shall despatch you to the abode of Yama with sharp arrows."

sanskrit: adya te maccharaiś chinnaṃ śiro jvalitakuṇḍalam kravyādā vyapakarṣantu vikīrṇaṃ raṇapāṃsuṣu
english: "Today let flesh-eating creatures drag away your head, severed by my arrows, its blazing earrings scattered in the dust of the battlefield."

sanskrit: nipatyorasi gṛdhrās te kṣitau kṣiptasya rāvaṇa pibantu rudhiraṃ tarṣād bāṇaśalyāntarothitam
english: "Let vultures alight on your chest, O Rāvaṇa, as you lie cast on the ground, and drink thirstily the blood oozing from the wounds of arrow-shafts."

sanskrit: adya madbāṇābhinnasya gatāsoḥ patitasya te karṣantv antrāṇi patagā garutmanta ivoragān
english: "Today let birds tear out your entrails as you lie slain, pierced by my arrows and fallen — as Garutmats tear serpents."

sanskrit: ity evaṃ sa vadan vīro rāmaḥ śatrunibarhaṇaḥ rākṣasendraṃ samīpasthaṃ śaravarṣair avākirat
english: Speaking thus, the heroic Rāma, destroyer of foes, rained down a shower of arrows on the lord of rākṣasas who stood nearby.

sanskrit: babhūva dviguṇaṃ vīryaṃ balaṃ harṣaś ca saṃyuge rāmasyāstrabalaṃ caiva śatror nidhanakāṅkṣiṇaḥ
english: Rāma's valour, strength, exhilaration in combat, and the power of his weapons all doubled as he longed for the death of his foe.

sanskrit: prādurbabhūvur astrāṇi sarvāṇi viditātmanaḥ praharṣāc ca mahātejāḥ śīghrahastataro 'bhavat
english: All weapons appeared of their own accord for that self-knowing one, and in his elation that greatly splendid hero became swifter of hand.

sanskrit: śubhāny etāni cihnāni vijñāyātmagatāni saḥ bhūya evārdayad rāmo rāvaṇaṃ rākṣasāntakṛt
english: Recognising these auspicious signs as dwelling within himself, Rāma, the destroyer of rākṣasas, assailed Rāvaṇa with renewed vigour.

sanskrit: harīṇāṃ cāśmanikaraiḥ śaravarṣaiś ca rāghavāt hanyamāno daśagrīvo vighūrṇahṛdayo 'bhavat
english: Struck by the monkeys' showers of rocks and by Rāghava's showers of arrows, Daśagrīva reeled at heart.

sanskrit: yadā ca śastraṃ nārebhe na vyakarṣac charāsanam nāsya pratyakarod vīryaṃ viklavenāntarātmanā
english: When he could no longer wield a weapon, could no longer draw his bow, could no longer display his valour — his inner spirit overcome with distress—

sanskrit: kṣiptāś cāpi śarās tena śastrāṇi vividhāni ca na raṇārthāya vartante mṛtyukāle 'bhivartataḥ
english: —even the arrows and various weapons he had hurled no longer availed him in battle, for the time of death was approaching.

sanskrit: sūtas tu rathanetāsya tadavasthaṃ nirīkṣya tam śanair yuddhād asaṃbhānto rathaṃ tasyāpavāhayat
english: His charioteer, the driver of his car, observing him in that condition, quietly and without panic drove his chariot away from the battle.

sanskrit: sa tu mohāt susaṃkruddhaḥ kṛtāntabalacoditaḥ krodhasaṃraktanayano rāvaṇo sūtam abravīt
english: But Rāvaṇa, deeply enraged out of his delusion, impelled by the power of Fate, his eyes reddened with anger, spoke to his charioteer:

sanskrit: hīnavīryam ivāśaktaṃ pauruṣeṇa vivarjitam bhīruṃ laghum ivāsattvaṃ vihīnam iva tejasā
english: "As though I were of diminished valour, as though powerless, as though deprived of manhood, as though a coward, as though of little account, as though destitute of spirit, as though stripped of splendour—

sanskrit: vimuktam iva māyābhir astrair iva bahiṣkṛtam mām avajñāya durbuddhe svayā buddhyā viceṣṭase
english: —as though abandoned by my powers of illusion, as though expelled by weapons — you disregard me, O evil-minded one, and act according to your own judgment!"

sanskrit: kimarthaṃ mām avajñāya macchandam anavekṣya ca tvayā śatrusamakṣaṃ me ratho 'yam apavāhitaḥ
english: "For what reason, ignoring me and disregarding my will, have you driven my chariot away in the presence of my enemy?"

sanskrit: tvayādya hi mamānārya cirakālasamārjitam yaśo vīryaṃ ca tejaś ca pratyayaś ca vināśitaḥ
english: "You, ignoble wretch, have today destroyed my fame, my valour, my splendour, and my reputation — all accumulated over long ages."

sanskrit: śatroḥ prakhyātavīryasya rañjanīyasya vikramaiḥ paśyato yuddhalubdho 'haṃ kṛtaḥ kāpuruṣas tvayā
english: "Before the eyes of the enemy, whose valour is renowned and whose courage inspires admiration, you have made me — eager for battle — appear a coward."

sanskrit: yas tvaṃ ratham imaṃ mohān na codvahasi durmate satyo 'yaṃ pratitarko me pareṇa tvam upaskṛtaḥ
english: "You who in your delusion do not drive this chariot forward, O evil-minded one — my suspicion is confirmed: you have been suborned by the enemy."

sanskrit: na hīdaṃ vidyate karma suhṛdo hitakāṅkṣiṇaḥ ripūṇāṃ sadṛśaṃ caitan na tvayaitat svanuṣṭhitam
english: "This act is not that of a friend who seeks one's good; it resembles the act of enemies; and what you have done is not properly done."

sanskrit: nivartaya rathaṃ śīghraṃ yāvan nāpaiti me ripuḥ yadi vāpy uṣito 'si tvaṃ smaryante yadi vā guṇāḥ
english: "Turn the chariot back quickly before my enemy escapes — if you have any decency left, if you still remember your virtues."

sanskrit: evaṃ paruṣam uktas tu hitabuddhir abuddhinā abravīd rāvaṇaṃ sūto hitaṃ sānunayaṃ vacaḥ
english: Thus harshly addressed by the senseless one, the charioteer — who sought his master's good — spoke beneficent and conciliatory words to Rāvaṇa:

sanskrit: na bhīto 'smi na mūḍho 'smi nopajapto 'smi śatrubhiḥ na pramatto na niḥsneho vismṛtā na ca satkriyā
english: "I am not afraid, nor am I confused, nor have I been suborned by enemies; I am not negligent, nor am I lacking in affection, nor have I forgotten my duty."

sanskrit: mayā tu hitakāmena yaśaś ca parirakṣatā snehapraskannamanasā priyam ity apriyaṃ kṛtam
english: "Rather, by me who desires your welfare and guards your glory, whose mind overflows with affection — what seemed unpleasant was done out of love."

sanskrit: nāsminn arthe mahārāja tvaṃ māṃ priyahite ratam kaś cil laghur ivānāryo doṣato gantum arhasi
english: "In this matter, O great king, you should not fault me who am devoted to your good — treating me like some ignoble wretch of low account."

sanskrit: śrūyatām abhidhāsyāmi yannimittaṃ mayā rathaḥ nadīvega ivāmbhobhiḥ saṃyuge vinivartitaḥ
english: "Hear me — I shall tell you the reason why I turned the chariot back in battle, like a current of water turned back by a flood."

sanskrit: śramaṃ tavāvagacchāmi mahatā raṇakarmaṇā na hi te vīra saumukhyaṃ praharṣaṃ vopadhāraye
english: "I perceived the great fatigue you suffer from the exertion of battle; I do not observe in you, O hero, either brightness of countenance or exhilaration."

sanskrit: rathodvahanakhinnāś ca ta ime rathavājinaḥ dīnā gharmapariśrāntā gāvo varṣahatā iva
english: "And these chariot-horses, wearied by the effort of pulling the car, are spent, exhausted by the heat, like cattle beaten down by rain."

sanskrit: nimittāni ca bhūyiṣṭhaṃ yāni prādurbhavanti naḥ teṣu teṣv abhipanneṣu lakṣayāmy apradakṣiṇam
english: "And the many omens that keep appearing around us — in each and every one of them I discern inauspiciousness."

sanskrit: deśakālau ca vijñeyau lakṣaṇānīṅgitāni ca dainyaṃ harṣaś ca khedaś ca rathinaś ca balābalam
english: "Place and time must be gauged, as must signs and indications, the dejection, exhilaration, and fatigue of the chariot-warrior, and the strength and weakness of both sides."

sanskrit: sthalanimnāni bhūmeś ca samāni viṣamāṇi ca yuddhakālaś ca vijñeyaḥ parasyāntaradarśanam
english: "The high and low ground, the level and uneven terrain, the right moment for battle — these must be assessed, as must the watching for an opening in the enemy."

sanskrit: upayānāpayāne ca sthānaṃ pratyapasarpaṇam sarvam etad rathasthena jñeyaṃ rathakuṭumbinā
english: "Advance and retreat, standing firm and falling back — all of this must be understood by one who rides a chariot, by one who governs a chariot."

sanskrit: tava viśrāmahetos tu tathaiṣāṃ rathavājinām raudraṃ varjayatā khedaṃ kṣamaṃ kṛtam idaṃ mayā
english: "For your rest and for that of these chariot-horses, avoiding a terrible reverse — what I have done here is proper."

sanskrit: na mayā svecchayā vīra ratho 'yam apavāhitaḥ bhartṛsnehaparītena mayedaṃ yatkṛtaṃ vibho
english: "This chariot was not driven away by me out of self-will, O hero; what I have done, O lord, was done out of love for my master."

sanskrit: ājñāpaya yathātattvaṃ vakṣyasy ariniṣūdana tat kariṣyāmy ahaṃ vīraṃ gatānṛṇyena cetasā
english: "Command me as you truly see fit, O destroyer of enemies — I shall do it with a heart free of all obligation."

sanskrit: saṃtuṣṭas tena vākyena rāvaṇas tasya sāratheḥ praśasyainaṃ bahuvidhaṃ yuddhalubdho 'bravīd idam
english: Satisfied with those words of his charioteer, Rāvaṇa, eager for battle, praised him in many ways and spoke thus:

sanskrit: rathaṃ śīghram imaṃ sūta rāghavābhimukhaṃ kuru nāhatvā samare śatrūn nivartiṣyati rāvaṇaḥ
english: "Quickly, O charioteer, turn this chariot to face Rāghava — Rāvaṇa will not turn back without slaying his enemies in battle."

sanskrit: evam uktvā tatas tuṣṭo rāvaṇo rākṣaseśvaraḥ dadau tasya śubhaṃ hy ekaṃ hastābharaṇam uttamam
english: Having spoken thus, Rāvaṇa, the satisfied lord of rākṣasas, gave him a single auspicious and supremely fine arm-ornament.

sanskrit: tato drutaṃ rāvaṇavākyacoditaḥ pracodayām āsa hayān sa sārathiḥ sa rākṣasendrasya tato mahārathaḥ kṣaṇena rāmasya raṇāgrato 'bhavat
english: Then swiftly, urged on by Rāvaṇa's command, the charioteer drove the horses forward; and the great chariot of the lord of rākṣasas was, in a moment, once again at the fore of the battle against Rāma.
